statement.p: Find the slope of the tangent line to the ellipse \displaystyle \frac{x^2}{4} + \frac{y^2}{25} = 1 at the point (x,y).
Are there any points where the slope is not defined? (Enter them as comma-separated ordered-pairs, e.g., (1,3), (-2,5). Enter none if there are no such points.)

static.solution:
\frac{2}{4} x + \frac{2}{25} y \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, so the slope is {dy\over dx} = -\frac{25 x}{4 y}.
The slope is not defined anywhere along the line y=0. This ellipse intersects that line in two places, (-2,0) and (2,0). (These are the ``ends'' of the ellipse where the tangent is vertical.)
